design_envelope.status: PLACEHOLDER design envelope (owner amendment of 14 Nov 2026 22:42), not canon
design_envelope.note: The only canon number is speed 1.0 = 44.704 m/s. Every band in this file is written against this envelope and moves if the envelope moves.

conventions.frame: Each team uses its own frame: u = metres from its own goal line toward the attacked goal (0 to 100); v = lateral metres from the centre line, positive to the right when facing the attacked goal (-50 to 50).
conventions.goal_arc: Polar about a goal centre. range_m = distance from the goal centre. bearing_deg: 0 is straight out from the goal toward midfield, positive to the right as the team faces its attacked goal.
conventions.ball_rel: Relative to the athlete's believed ball position. du_m positive = toward the attacked goal. dv_m = lateral.
conventions.line_rel: At a restart, relative to the restraining line: the ball line at a tackle or turnover scrimmage; at a 40 m scrimmage, the ball line for the restarting team and its own 40 m line for the defending team. du_m negative = on the athlete's own side.
conventions.mirror: With mirror or spread "mirror", the lateral or bearing band is a magnitude and instances are placed on both sides.
conventions.toss_in: At a toss-in slots use their live-play anchors, with opponents 3 m clear of the spot.
conventions.beliefs: Every anchor is evaluated by the athlete from his own believed positions. No anchor is a position the engine places anyone at.
conventions.bands: ELITE 0.90 or more; KEY 0.85 or more; SUPPORT 0.75 to 0.80; BASE 0.70. Body gates sit near the middle of the range. A slot has one KEY rating, or two where the method needs both in one body.

classes.EXPRESSIBLE NOW: Native v0/3 can run it today with no code change. In practice this means the parameter is one of the 16 team-wide PolicyParams fields, with the same value for every teammate.
classes.NEEDS COORDINATION: The engine mechanics, intent kinds and view fields exist in Native v0/3, but the athlete does not hold the value: it differs by slot, replaces a constant in cognition, or only works if teammates hold the same plan. Needs the pre-match playbook of TACTIC_INTERFACE.md and cognition that reads it. No physics or rules change.
classes.NEEDS ENGINE WORK: Needs something the engine, port or rules layer does not provide in Native v0/3: ratings and bodies per athlete (ATTRIBUTE_STEP_SPEC.md), athlete-chosen release speed, voluntary off-ball contact, or a public signal missing from the view.

carrier.bias_pass.meaning: Added to the value of every pass option.

carrier.bias_shoot.meaning: Added to the value of the shoot option.

carrier.pass_min_clearance_m.meaning: Pass options whose believed lane clearance is below this are dropped.

carrier.shot_range_max_m.meaning: Largest believed distance to goal at which a throw at goal is an option.

carrier.shot_range_min_m.meaning: Smallest believed distance to goal at which a throw at goal is an option.
carrier.shot_range_min_m.reason: v0/3 cognition has no minimum-distance filter on the shoot option; the playbook value must be read in cognition.

carrier.finish_pref.meaning: Preference weights over scoring methods: carry in, close throw (under 10 m), mid throw (10 to 20 m), deep throw (20 m or more).
carrier.finish_pref.reason: v0/3 values one shoot option and one carry option with no distance bands; the bands need playbook weights in cognition. Release distance is the athlete's own believed distance.

carrier.shot_speed_frac.meaning: Release speed of a throw at goal as a fraction of the thrower's own maximum.
carrier.shot_speed_frac.reason: v0/3 releases every pass and shot at min(27, max) m/s and 1.6 m height (R10 F-4). Athlete-chosen release speed and a per-athlete maximum from throw_power are engine and attribute-step work.

carrier.pass_len_band_m.reason: v0/3 pass options are fixed to a believed 4 to 34 m at 27 m/s. Bands beyond 34 m, or needing a faster ball, depend on athlete-chosen release speed. A band inside 4 to 34 m would need only the playbook.

carrier.touch_time_max_s.meaning: Longest time a ball holder outside the Keeper Zone keeps the ball before passing or throwing. 30 means no limit.
carrier.touch_time_max_s.reason: v0/3 has no own-possession timer. Needs an own-action memory of when I gained the ball (own knowledge) and a playbook threshold.

carrier.contact_response.meaning: Preference weights among run through, dodge and brace when a tackler is believed to be arriving.
carrier.contact_response.reason: The three intents exist in v0/3 but are chosen from constants (THREAT_HORIZON_S, DODGE_MIN_S, BRACE_LOAD). The playbook must replace them.

carrier.first_tackle_bank_m.meaning: While the tackle count is 0, the carrier accepts contact only inside this distance of the attacked goal; farther out he prefers to dodge or pass. 100 means anywhere.
carrier.first_tackle_bank_m.reason: Needs the public tackle count in the athlete's view. v0/3 Signals carry no tackle count.

carrier.dribble_use.meaning: When the one dribble per possession is used.
carrier.dribble_use.reason: The dribble intent exists; v0/3 uses it only when no teammate is believed visible. A playbook rule must choose it.

tempo.shot_window_s.meaning: Seconds into the 30 s play clock in which the team prefers to take its scoring attempt.
tempo.shot_window_s.reason: The possession clock is a public signal in the view. v0/3 has only a fixed +5 shoot value in the first 5 s. Needs playbook values.

tempo.must_shoot_remaining_s.meaning: With this much play clock left, the ball holder attempts to score from where he is.
tempo.must_shoot_remaining_s.reason: Same public clock; no such rule in v0/3 cognition.

tempo.snap_delay_s.meaning: Seconds the snapper waits inside the legal 10 s snap window, when leading and otherwise.
tempo.snap_delay_s.reason: v0/3 releases as soon as a legal throw exists. Score is public. Assumes waiting inside the legal window is not delay of game (Q-TAC-4).

tempo.hold_own_half_until_remaining_s.meaning: The team keeps the ball in its own half until this much play clock remains. 30 means it does not hold.
tempo.hold_own_half_until_remaining_s.reason: A position and hold rule from the public clock; needs the playbook. Its purpose (no legal arrow target outside the Archer's own half) rests on a ratified rule that v0/3 does not enforce.

off.first_action_max_s.meaning: After gaining a live ball, longest time before the first forward pass or carry.
off.first_action_max_s.reason: Needs an own-action memory of when I gained the ball and a playbook threshold.

off.short_field_trigger_m.meaning: If possession is gained within this distance of the attacked goal, the team attempts to score at once. 0 means never.
off.short_field_trigger_m.reason: Own believed position and a playbook threshold.

pos.ball_att.meaning: In possession: pull toward the believed ball.

pos.ball_def.meaning: Out of possession: pull toward the believed ball.

pos.goal_att.meaning: In possession: pull toward the attacked goal.

pos.goal_def.meaning: Out of possession: pull toward own goal.

pos.spread.meaning: Prefer distance from the nearest believed teammate.

pos.opp_att.meaning: In possession: prefer distance from the nearest believed opponent.

pos.opp_def.meaning: Out of possession: prefer closeness to the nearest believed opponent.

pos.lane.meaning: In possession: prefer an open believed lane from the carrier.

pos.edge_zone.meaning: Penalty for standing near a field edge or inside either Keeper Zone.

pos.anchor_pull.meaning: Weight of the athlete's own slot anchor against the nine belief-driven terms above. 0 means the anchor is ignored.
pos.anchor_pull.reason: There is no anchor in v0/3. The weight is read from the playbook by cognition; it sets how strongly the plan pulls and is the same unsearched value for every style.

zone.entry_mode.meaning: How attackers use the attacked Keeper Zone.
zone.entry_mode.reason: v0/3 has one behaviour (a position penalty for zones). A mode needs the playbook.

zone.dwell_max_s.meaning: An attacker leaves the zone when his own residence reaches this. Canon limit is 5 s.
zone.dwell_max_s.reason: v0/3 leaves at a fixed 3.0 s. Own residence time is already in the view; the playbook must supply the threshold.

zone.occupancy_target.meaning: Number of attackers the team tries to keep inside the zone in settled offence.
zone.occupancy_target.reason: Each athlete can count believed teammates inside, but who goes in next is a shared arrangement held in the playbook.

zone.min_outside_s.meaning: Self-imposed minimum time outside before the same attacker re-enters.
zone.min_outside_s.reason: Own knowledge and a playbook value. Canon states no minimum time outside (Q-TAC-1).

zone.entry_stagger_s.meaning: Offset between the entries of paired attackers in a rotation.
zone.entry_stagger_s.reason: A timing agreement between teammates with no live channel: each acts on his own belief of the partner leaving.

block.wedge.meaning: Lead blockers make legal off-ball contact (shoulder, push; no grip) ahead of the carrier.
block.wedge.reason: Native has no voluntary off-ball contact intents (Q-HAND-1). Without them the wedge is only bodies in the way.

screen.arrow_screen.meaning: A screener stands between the Archer platform and a paired thrower.
screen.arrow_screen.reason: Position only, held in the playbook and paired with one teammate. Rests on arrow-body collision, which the engine has. Effect unmeasured.

def.bias_press.meaning: Added to the value of closing on the believed carrier.

def.bias_pursue.meaning: Added to the value of pursuing a loose ball.

def.scheme.reason: A scheme is the set of slot anchors and marking rules below; it exists only if every teammate holds the same chart.

def.pressers_max.meaning: How many defenders close on the carrier at once.
def.pressers_max.reason: v0/3 lets the two believed-nearest press (a constant).

def.press_line_m.meaning: The carrier is engaged only when he is within this distance of the defending goal. 100 means everywhere.
def.press_line_m.reason: Own believed positions and a playbook value; no such line in v0/3.

def.commit_gap_m.meaning: Believed gap at which a pressing defender commits to contact.
def.commit_gap_m.reason: TACKLE_COMMIT_M = 6.0 is a constant in v0/3.

def.contain_gap_m.meaning: Gap a containing defender keeps to the carrier.
def.contain_gap_m.reason: Containing without contact is a position choice; needs the playbook.

def.takedown_line_m.meaning: A takedown is chosen only when the carrier is within this distance of the defending goal. 100 means anywhere.
def.takedown_line_m.reason: Own believed positions and a playbook value.

def.contact_by_area.meaning: Contact a defender chooses by area: beyond the takedown line (midfield), inside it but outside the zone (arc), inside the own Keeper Zone (zone).
def.contact_by_area.reason: Wrap and takedown intents exist in v0/3; the area is the athlete's own believed position.

def.contact_at_count1.meaning: Contact chosen once the offence has used its first tackle.
def.contact_at_count1.reason: Needs the public tackle count in the athlete's view. v0/3 Signals carry none.

def.holdup_drive.meaning: Direction a wrapping defender drives the carrier.
def.holdup_drive.reason: The aim of a wrapping defender is his own intent. Whether a wrap can move or hold a carrier is engine physics as built, unmeasured.

archer.eagerness.meaning: Added to the value of every draw-and-release option.

archer.target_priority.meaning: Relative value of legal targets: the believed carrier, the receiver nearest the goal, any other legal attacker.
archer.target_priority.reason: v0/3 uses constants (carrier 3.0, others 1.6 minus 0.04 per metre from the ball). The Archer is one athlete, so no teammate is involved.

keeper.depth_m.meaning: How far off the goal line the Keeper sets.
keeper.depth_m.reason: v0/3 Keeper depth is clamp(0.25 x distance, 1, 4), a constant rule.

keeper.distribution.meaning: What the Keeper does with a secured ball.
keeper.distribution.reason: Target choice needs the slot chart. A long outlet beyond 34 m also depends on carrier.pass_len_band_m.

restart.scrim_play.meaning: Set play at a Contact Scrimmage with the ball.
restart.scrim_play.reason: v0/3 throws to a believed teammate 4 to 34 m away and two teammates make themselves throwable. A named play is a shared arrangement.

restart.snap40_play.meaning: Set play at the 40 m scrimmage after conceding.

restart.toss_play.reason: As restart.scrim_play. A tossed ball cannot score until another player controls it.

restart.def_alignment.meaning: Defensive alignment at an opponent restart.
restart.def_alignment.reason: Slot anchors relative to the restraining line; shared chart.

restart.taker_slot.meaning: Slot that prefers to take 40 m scrimmages and toss-ins. The snapper after a tackle is fixed by rule.
restart.taker_slot.reason: v0/3 claim goes to the believed-nearest teammate. A slot preference needs the others to hold back.

hunt.contestant_slot.meaning: Slot whose holder claims the Hunt.
hunt.contestant_slot.reason: v0/3 admits a claim from any field player. Naming one slot needs the others to abstain. It matters only once athletes differ.

hunt.win_action.meaning: What the contestant does on winning the ball.
hunt.win_action.reason: An individual choice of the contestant; needs the playbook.

slot.anchor.meaning: Where a slot stands in each situation (offence, defence, own restart, opponent restart, Hunt), relative to ball, field or goal.
slot.anchor.reason: v0/3 has no slots or anchors (native/README: no positional role or formation grid). Each athlete needs its own slot and anchor in a playbook, and the shape exists only if all teammates hold the same chart.

slot.requires.meaning: Minimum rating and body bands for a slot.
slot.requires.reason: Native v0/3 gives every athlete rating 0.70 and one body and reads no roster (ATTRIBUTE_STEP_SPEC.md).

slot.prefers.meaning: Weights used to rank candidates for a slot.

assignment.rule.meaning: Pre-match rule that fills slots from a supplied roster by rating band.
assignment.rule.reason: A step outside the engine, but there is nothing to assign until rosters carry ratings, and the harness has no per-athlete playbook input.

subs.policy.reason: As built: substitutes only cover exclusions and disqualifications. TACTICS-0 keeps the same ten field starters in every phase.

assignment_rule.name: assign by rating band from a supplied roster
assignment_rule.input: A roster table: id, role (field, keeper, archer), the ratings on a 0 to 1 scale, height_m, mass_kg. At least 10 field athletes, 1 keeper, 1 archer.
steps: Keeper and Archer slots take the highest-scoring athlete of that role. Field athletes never fill them (canon).
Field slot instances are taken in the tactic's slot order, which is its priority order.
An athlete is in band for a slot if he meets every minimum in requires.

In-band placement is a maximum matching between instances and in-band athletes (augmenting paths; instances in priority order; candidates in descending slot score; ties by roster order), so no in-band placement is lost to an earlier choice.
Slot score = sum over prefers of weight x rating, with height and mass rescaled to the 0.60 to 1.00 band over the envelope ranges.
An instance left empty takes the highest-scoring unassigned field athlete and is flagged under band, with each shortfall listed.
Status: BROKEN if any slot has fewer in-band instances than its fail_below_in_band; FULL if every instance is in band; otherwise DEGRADED.
The remaining athletes are the bench. A substitute takes the slot of the athlete he replaces.

plays.default: As built in Native v0/3: the taker throws to a believed teammate 4 to 34 m from the spot.
plays.quick_swing: The taker throws 6 to 8 m back and to one side to a named handler slot, who starts the normal offence. All teammates start behind the ball line.
plays.wedge_snap: The taker throws 5 m straight back to a RAM. The PLOWs stand 0.8 to 1.5 m behind the ball line in a V and move on the release. All teammates start behind the ball line.
plays.zone_stack: The taker throws 7 m back to a HUB. DARTs stand wide on the ball line and enter the zone on the release, in their rotation order.
plays.safe_reset: The taker throws 8 m back to a METRONOME and the team re-forms its passing diamond. The taker waits tempo.snap_delay_s inside the legal window first.
plays.go_routes: The taker throws 7 m back to a CANNON. BOLTs stand on the ball line at wide, centre, wide and sprint on the release; the CANNON throws long into the space ahead of one of them.
plays.short_toss: The thrower tosses 6 to 10 m infield to the nearest named handler slot. The thrower may not recover the ball himself and the ball cannot score until another player controls it.
plays.line_toss: The thrower tosses up the boundary to a BOLT running into space. Same toss-in limits.
plays.def:shell: All field defenders stand 5.5 m or more on their own side of the restraining line, between ball and goal.
plays.def:man_up: Each field defender stands 5.5 m on his own side of the restraining line, opposite one attacker, and closes on the release.
plays.def:ring: RINGs stand on the 21 to 25 m arc if the spot is outside it, otherwise 5.5 m behind the line; SHADOWs 5.5 m behind the line opposite the likely receivers.
plays.def:gate: CLAMPs and GATEs take their arc posts if the spot is outside the zone, otherwise 5.5 m behind the line; DENYs opposite the likely receivers at 5.5 m.
plays.def:wall: RAMs and PLOWs stand shoulder to shoulder 5.5 m behind the restraining line; FLANKs and TAILs outside them.

restart_rules: After a tackle the tackled carrier is the snapper and the tackler stands opposite him or 5 m behind (canon); no play names them.
Everyone else starts on his own side of the ball line (offside rule).
At a 40 m scrimmage after a score every athlete starts at or behind his own 40 m line.
No defender stands within 5 m of an opponent before the ball is live (5 m marking), so every defensive anchor is 5.5 m or more behind the restraining line.
The snap is released inside the 10 s window; a toss within 4 s of ready, with opponents 3 m clear.

tactics.name: Arc Siege
tactics.idea: Keep every attacker outside the Keeper Zone on the 21 to 24 m arc, move the ball by quick passes, and score with hard throws released from 20 m or more. The bet is that a fast, accurate deep throw beats a Keeper who has no help, because defenders may not wait inside the zone without an attacker to mark.

slots.what: Deep thrower: catches on the arc and throws at goal from 20 m or more.

understaffed.effect: FAILURE below two in band: a slower or less accurate deep throw gives the Keeper time and the style has no other scoring route. With two of three in band one arc sector goes unused (graceful).

strengths: Never puts an attacker on the 5 s zone limit.
Keeps the defence out of the zone by rule: a defender may stay there only within 5 m of an attacker.
Deep throws are the highest-valued throws on the provisional scale (4).
weaknesses: Every attacker is a legal arrow target for the whole possession.
Needs two rare players: high throw power and high accuracy together.
A saved or missed throw is a live ball with eight attackers 70 m or more from their own goal.
Under the flat scoring now in force a deep goal is worth no more than a close one.
canon_checks: No attacker waits inside the zone; a rebound chase leaves within 2 s (limit 5 s).
Screens are stationary bodies; any contact stays in the legal band (below the neck, above the hip, no grip).
No pass or carry goes back into the own Keeper Zone (ZR-C, ZR-T).

edge_over.why: Count's shell waits on the arc and commits late (4 m). In-band GUNs release from 21 to 24 m over it, and Count's long possessions do not lower the quality of Arc's attempts.
Lock's trap needs a zone entry and Arc does not enter. Lock contains outside its takedown line, so GUNs release unhurried.

struggles_against.why: Arc's throwers and feeders stand outside the zone in the Archer's half for the whole possession: up to five freezes on near-stationary targets, and as built a frozen ball holder drops the ball.
Arc needs time to set five players on the arc and circulate. The press tackles the first receiver before the arc forms, and GUN and SCREEN profiles are not chosen for escaping pressure.

no_prediction.question: Neither method touches the other's. Outside finishing against man marking, inside finishing against an arc shell: no prediction.
Ram's Wall stands at 24 to 28 m, right where GUNs release, but its heavy profiles are slow to close: no prediction.
Arc attacks ten against seven, but every saved throw is a live ball with BOLTs already high. Which is larger is the question.

tactics.name: Zone Waves
tactics.idea: The 5 s limit is counted per attacker and "at a time", so the team rotates attackers through the Keeper Zone in short visits of 3.5 s and always has fresh ones inside. Attackers inside the zone are not legal arrow targets, and they finish with close and mid throws or a carry.

understaffed.effect: FAILURE with none in band: entries are fed late or to the wrong man and attackers burn their 5 s without the ball. With one in band the feed comes from one side only (graceful).

strengths: Finishers are sheltered from the Archer while inside the zone.
Close and mid throws give the Keeper the least time.
Defenders who follow an attacker in must leave again when he leaves, or become unmarked.
weaknesses: The rotation is a timing agreement with no live channel; each athlete acts on his own belief of where his partner is.
Only 1.5 s of margin on the limit: any hold-up inside the zone risks a turnover.
Close and mid throws are the lowest-valued throws on the provisional scale (2 and 3).
HUBs outside the arc remain arrow targets.
canon_checks: Every visit ends at 3.5 s, inside the 5 s limit; expiry would be a turnover.
Reads the Rulebook wording "at most 5 seconds at a time" as a fresh 5 s on re-entry. Canon states no minimum time outside; the plan imposes 1.0 s on itself (PLACEHOLDER, Q-TAC-1).
No contact on the Keeper inside his zone.

edge_over.why: Attackers inside the zone are not legal arrow targets and Wave keeps its finishers there. Anvil's shadows contain without tackling, which gives the rotation time.
Ram's Wall is staffed by heavy RAM and PLOW profiles. A rotation every 3.5 s makes them follow attackers in and out of the zone or stand unmarked.

struggles_against.why: Wave enters the zone by design with 1.5 s of margin. A hold-up of 1.5 s turns a visit into a residence turnover.

no_prediction.question: Neither method touches the other's. Outside finishing against man marking, inside finishing against an arc shell: no prediction.
The press may break the rotation before it forms, or its man marking may be dragged in and out of the zone: no prediction.
Count's shell must follow attackers into the zone or leave them free; whether it copes is not something reasoning settles.
Wave commits five or six attackers deep, but many of its turnovers are dead balls (residence): no prediction.

tactics.name: Carry Train
tactics.idea: One power carrier runs behind a wedge of blockers and the team spends its one free tackle on purpose, close to goal. From the scrimmage that follows, a second wedge run from 10 to 20 m carries the ball over the goal plane in under 5 s.
tactics.formation: 2 RAM (carrier and relief), 4 PLOW in a V ahead of the ball, 2 FLANK wide, 2 TAIL behind

slots.what: Power carrier: carries into contact and stays up.

understaffed.effect: FAILURE with none in band: a carrier who goes down on first contact uses both tackles before the arc. With one in band there is no relief carrier (graceful).

Wave enters the zone by design with 1.5 s of margin. A hold-up of 1.5 s turns a visit into a residence turnover.
Ram puts the whole possession on one carrier who runs 40 m or more outside the zone: the Archer's first target. As built a freeze makes him drop the ball.
Ram wants its free first tackle close to goal. The press forces it far out, leaving a second run of 50 m or more with no tackle left.
Count's shell commits late and avoids contact; a wedge reaches the arc at speed and needs under 2 s inside. Ram's Wall tackles hard and a 20 s possession offers it many chances.
Strike defends with seven, so the wedge meets fewer tacklers. Ram's turnovers are mostly dead balls, which deny Strike the live gain it needs.
The trap needs about 5 s of hold-up. A wedge-led carry needs under 2 s from arc to goal plane, and Lock chooses not to ground a carrier in the zone at count 0.

Once Count crosses halfway it still holds the ball for 10 s or more outside the zone, the longest exposure of any style. The edge is larger in Native v0/3, which does not enforce the own-half arrow rule.
Strike attempts within 8 s, before the Archer has released more than a few arrows, and its long passes travel over shadows who are containing, not tackling.
Count's short passes are exactly what man pressure contests, and Count may not retreat into its own zone, so the press compresses it against the arc.
The press commits eight players upfield man to man. One completed long pass to a BOLT beats all of them, with two SWEEPs behind.
Count gives up few live turnovers and keeps three REST players behind the ball, so the BOLTs waiting high receive little; and Count attacks a seven-player defence.
Count attempts with 3 to 8 s left. A hold-up at the door squeezes it between the zone limit and the play clock with no time to recycle.
Lock does not press upfield, so its defenders are at the arc when the long pass arrives. The break ends in a zone entry against a set trap.
Neither method touches the other's. Outside finishing against man marking, inside finishing against an arc shell: no prediction.

Arc attacks ten against seven, but every saved throw is a live ball with BOLTs already high. Which is larger is the question.

Wave commits five or six attackers deep, but many of its turnovers are dead balls (residence): no prediction.
